summary: Official Delta State sources establish local/state land-registration custody and an ongoing digitization/parcel-mapping programme, but no anonymous public Sapele parcel ID plus polygon response was verified. No sample GeoJSON is retained; runtime remains held.
queryOutcomes: Separate English and Nigerian-English/Pidgin-oriented discovery queries and actual result URLs are recorded in city-6240-sapele.json. Results distinguished Delta State Ministry of Lands & Survey/D'LARMS custody from federal surveying information, third-party material, and historical Gazette evidence.
requestOutcomes: TLS-verified bounded GETs returned HTTP 200 HTML from Delta State MDA Services, HTTP 200 PDF from the official BERAP document, HTTP 200 HTML from OSGOF, and HTTP 200 HTML from third-party map/information pages. No official viewer configuration, schema, CRS or safe ID-plus-geometry response was exposed. No login, credentials, private token, CAPTCHA/Cloudflare bypass, unsafe field request or TLS disablement was used.

Official Delta State BERAP 2025 PDF describing D'LARMS/digitization and parcel mapping

scopeLimits: Exact WUP point [5.87952425350026, 5.68865672791976] was preserved in latitude/longitude order and never shifted; no exact-point hit/miss inference was made.
No Sapele boundary or complete citywide coverage was established for an open geometry service.
No parcel geometry, stable native parcel identity, source schema or CRS was retrieved or retained.
A state registry procedure and a digitization programme are not proof of an open vector parcel API.
A timeout, login wall, map extent miss or unusable UI is not evidence of citywide cadastral absence.
No owner, address, titleholder, contact, tax/account or other personal/sensitive fields were requested or retained.
Packet completion is research evidence only and does not qualify or admit a runtime adapter; serial reviewer qualification remains pending.
